1.title: 'Is there no God in Israel?'
1.text: Injured, king Ahaziah sent to consult Baal-zebub, god of Ekron. Elijah intercepts with the cutting question: 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that ye go to enquire of Baal-zebub?'

1.question: Whom did king Ahaziah send to consult about his illness?
options: Baal-zebub, god of Ekron
Milcom, the god of the Ammonites
Astaroth, the goddess of the Sidonians
Chemosh, the god of Moab

1.question: What did Elijah announce to the king for consulting an idol?
options: That he would not leave his bed, but die
That he would rise and reign for many years
That his kingdom would extend over all Israel
That his sons would inherit the whole throne

1.question: What happened to the first two companies of fifty soldiers?
options: Fire from heaven consumed them
They were taken prisoner to Samaria
A storm scattered them across the mountain
They returned without Elijah

1.question: What happened to Ahaziah, according to Elijah's word?
options: He died, leaving no son to succeed him
He recovered and reigned twenty more years
He was deposed by his own royal subjects
He was healed of his grave illness

2.title: The chariot of fire
2.text: As they walked and talked, a chariot of fire with horses of fire parted them, and Elijah went up into heaven by a whirlwind — one of the most extraordinary passages in the Old Testament.

2.question: Where did Elijah and Elisha pass as Elijah's end drew near?
options: Through Beth-el and Jericho, to the Jordan
Through Gilgal and Beth-el, all the way to Jerusalem
Through Samaria and Bethlehem, all the way to Egypt
Through Dan and Beersheba, to the north

2.question: What did Elisha ask of Elijah before he was taken up?
options: A double portion of his spirit
Authority to judge all the tribes of Israel
A place among the sons of the prophets
Healing from his severe leprosy

2.question: How was Elijah taken up to heaven?
options: In a chariot of fire and a whirlwind
In a very thick and brightly shining cloud
In a golden chariot drawn by two angels
In a deep vision during his sleep

2.question: What did Elisha do with salt to the waters of Jericho?
options: He healed them, making them wholesome
He cursed them in the name of the Lord
He multiplied them throughout the whole valley
He purified them with sacred fire

2.question: What happened to the youths who mocked Elisha?
options: Two bears came out of the woods against them
They were taken prisoner to the city of Jericho
Fire came down from heaven and consumed them completely
They were harshly cursed by Elijah himself

3.title: Valleys full of water
3.text: Elisha ordered ditches dug across the valley: 'Ye shall not see wind, neither rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water.' God provided with no visible sign — and the water would even deceive Moab.

3.question: What did Moab do after Ahab's death?
options: It rebelled against Israel
It allied with the Edomites
It increased the tribute of lambs
It sought help from Assyria

3.question: What problem did the three kings face in the wilderness?
options: They ran out of water for the army
The troops ran out of food for seven days
The horses died of thirst before the battle
There was a mutiny among the soldiers

3.question: What did Elisha command be done across the valley?
options: To dig many ditches to receive water
To sacrifice lambs upon a stone altar
To surround the Moabite camp at night
To send messengers to the Edomites

3.question: How did the water appear, according to Elisha?
options: It filled the valley without wind or rain
It sprang forth from a rock split open by Elisha's staff
It appeared suddenly after an earthquake split the ground
It came down like the morning dew at dawn

3.question: Why did the Moabites attack carelessly and were defeated?
options: They thought the reddened water was blood
They believed the enemy armies had fled during the night
They trusted false prophets who promised certain victory
They judged that the terrain favored their attack

4.title: Everyday miracles
4.text: The miracles of this chapter are domestic: a debt, a child, a spoiled meal, a famine. Elisha shows that God cares about the ordinary needs of people.

4.question: What happened to the indebted widow's oil?
options: It multiplied and filled every vessel, paying the debt
It dried up completely before filling every empty vessel
It turned into vinegar and was no longer useful at all
It spilled by accident and was all lost soon after

4.question: What did the Shunammite woman prepare for Elisha?
options: A room in her house, to host him
A large garden, to grow fresh herbs
A new altar, to offer sacrifices on
A full meal, every single day

4.question: What did Elisha promise the childless Shunammite?
options: That she would have a son the next year
That she would gain great riches before she died
That she would live many years in good health
That she would have a new house in Shunem

4.question: What happened to the Shunammite's son when he grew?
options: He got a head pain and died
He was wounded in battle and died
He fell ill with fever and recovered soon
He suddenly went blind

4.question: What did the Shunammite do when her son died?
options: She went to find Elisha without giving up
She buried him quietly in the garden of her house
She despaired and called all her neighbors
She blamed the prophet for everything

4.question: Whom did Elisha first send with his staff to the child?
options: Gehazi, his servant
A neighbor from the village
The Shunammite's husband
One of the reapers

4.question: What did Elisha himself do for the dead child?
options: He lay upon him, and the body grew warm
He prayed from afar, and nothing happened at once
He anointed him with holy oil, but he did not breathe
He carried him to the temple in Jerusalem

4.question: How did Elisha heal the poisoned stew ('death in the pot')?
options: He cast meal into the pot
He changed all the water in the pot
He only prayed for divine healing
He fasted for seven days

4.question: What did Elisha do with twenty loaves before a hundred men?
options: He multiplied them, and there was even some left
He divided them equally among all who were present
He refused them, since they were far too few for everyone
He stored them away for the following day

5.title: Healing through humble obedience
5.text: Naaman was offended by the simple command to wash in the Jordan — he expected a grand gesture. Only when he humbled himself and obeyed was he healed: his flesh became like a child's.

5.question: Who was Naaman, and what was his problem?
options: A Syrian commander who was a leper
A Syrian priest who was completely blind
A royal messenger who was completely deaf
An Egyptian captain badly wounded

5.question: Who told Naaman there was a prophet who could heal him?
options: A little Israelite servant girl
The king of Syria himself, his lord
Elisha himself, coming to visit him
An old priest from the temple

5.question: What did Elisha tell Naaman to do to be healed?
options: To dip seven times in the Jordan river
To offer plenty of gold and silver to the prophet
To fast for seven whole days and to pray
To climb the tall mountain and pray

5.question: What did Gehazi do after Naaman was healed and left?
options: He ran after him to take gifts in secret
He accompanied him to Syria to serve as a slave
He immediately told the king about Naaman's healing
He stayed quiet and still in his own house

5.question: What happened to Gehazi for his greed and lying?
options: Naaman's leprosy clung to him
He was expelled from the city in shame
He lost his job and his whole house
He was pardoned by Elisha

6.title: 'They that be with us are more'
6.text: Surrounded by the Syrian army, Elisha's servant was afraid. But the prophet prayed, and God opened his eyes: the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire around them.

6.question: What did Elisha do to the iron axe head that fell in the water?
options: He made it float
He bought another
He dived for it
He left it lost

6.question: How did Elisha help Israel's king against Syria?
options: He revealed the Syrian king's secret plans in advance
He summoned the prophets to pray for Israel's victory
He sent disguised spies to the Syrian king's military camp
He personally led the Israelite army in battle

6.question: What did the king of Syria do on learning Elisha was exposing him?
options: He had the city where he was (Dothan) surrounded
He sent messengers to negotiate the city's surrender
He ordered the army to withdraw immediately toward Damascus
He quickly sent gifts to appease Elisha

6.question: What did Elisha's servant see when God opened his eyes?
options: The mountain full of horses and chariots of fire
A great enemy army surrounding the entire city walls
Many mighty angels descending from heaven in glory
Nothing unusual in the surrounding hills

6.question: What did Elisha do with the blinded Syrian soldiers led to Samaria?
options: He fed them and sent them back in peace
He captured them and took them as prisoners of war
He enslaved them and forced them to serve in his army
He killed them all before the king of Israel

6.question: What happened in Samaria when Ben-hadad besieged it?
options: A terrible famine, even to cannibalism
A great plague that killed many inhabitants
A terrible fire that destroyed much of the city
A violent rebellion against the king

6.question: What did the king of Israel vow to do because of the famine?
options: To have Elisha beheaded
To surrender the city to the Syrians
To attack the Syrian army immediately
To pray daily in the temple

7.title: To see, but not to taste
7.text: When Elisha promised plenty the next day, an officer scoffed: 'Even if the Lord made windows in heaven?' Elisha answered that he would see it with his eyes, but not eat of it — and so it was.

7.question: What did Elisha prophesy about the famine in Samaria?
options: That the next day there would be plenty and cheap food
That the city would completely fall into Syrian hands soon
That fire would rain down from heaven on the whole besieged city
That the famine would last many more difficult years

7.question: Why did the Syrian army abandon their camp?
options: God made them hear a great army, and they fled
They were completely defeated in battle by Israel's soldiers
They caught a contagious plague that spread through the camp
They received direct orders from the king to retreat

7.question: What did the king of Israel suspect on hearing the camp was empty?
options: That it was a Syrian ambush
That it was a miracle sent by God to Israel
That it was a lie invented by the starving lepers
That it was just a strange dream

7.question: What happened to the officer who had doubted the prophecy?
options: He was trampled by the crowd at the gate
He was promoted to captain of the king's army
He fled the city before the crowd reached the gate
He repented and asked the king for forgiveness

8.title: Elisha weeps over the future
8.text: Foreseeing that Hazael would reign, Elisha fixed his gaze on him and wept — for he knew the evil Hazael would do to Israel. The prophecy was no prize, but an announcement of suffering.

8.question: What did the Shunammite recover by appealing to the king?
options: Her house and her land
An important position at the royal court
A large amount of gold and silver
Her long-lost only son

8.question: What did Elisha foresee about Hazael, in Damascus?
options: That he would become king of Syria
That he would die in battle against the Israelites
That he would convert to the God of Israel
That he would soon attack Egypt

8.question: What did Hazael do to become king?
options: He smothered king Ben-hadad and seized the throne
He won a decisive war against the entire Syrian army
He was elected by the council of wise Syrian elders
He bought the throne with much gold and silver

8.question: What was Jehoram's reign like in Judah?
options: He did evil, married to a daughter of Ahab's house
He was righteous and feared God like Jehoshaphat, his father
He faithfully restored the temple and abolished idolatry
His reign was brief, peaceful, and free of wars

8.question: What did Edom do in the time of Jehoram of Judah?
options: It revolted from Judah's rule
It formed a military alliance with the king of Israel
It attacked Syria and conquered several cities
It paid heavy tribute to Judah's king

8.question: What was Ahaziah, king of Judah, like?
options: He walked in the ways of Ahab's house
He was upright before the Lord all his life
He completely abolished idolatry throughout the kingdom
He reigned many years with great wisdom

9.title: The end of Jezebel
9.text: Fulfilling Elijah's prophecy, Jezebel was thrown from the window and dogs devoured her, leaving only the skull, feet and hands. Jehu was the instrument of judgment on Ahab's house.

9.question: For what did a young prophet anoint Jehu?
options: To be king of Israel and destroy Ahab's house
To be high priest and purify Israel's sanctuary
To free Israel entirely from the yoke of the king of Syria
To rebuild the altar destroyed by Jezebel

9.question: What was Jehu's mission on being anointed king?
options: To wipe out Ahab's house, avenging the prophets
Restore the worship of Baal throughout Israel's kingdom
Seal a lasting covenant of peace with Ahab's house
Collect tribute for the temple of Baal

9.question: What did the other officers do on learning of Jehu's anointing?
options: They proclaimed: 'Jehu is king!'
They refused to acknowledge him
They sent messengers to Joram
They shut all the city gates

9.question: How did Jehu advance toward Jezreel?
options: He drove furiously, like a madman
He marched slowly, surrounded by guards
He advanced in disguise, hiding his identity
He went on foot, without any haste

9.question: What did Jehu do to king Joram?
options: He killed him with an arrow, in Naboth's field
Imprisoned him in the palace until he starved to death
Exiled him to Syria, along with all his servants
He spared him and sent him back to Jezreel

9.question: What also happened to Ahaziah, king of Judah?
options: He fled, but was wounded and died
He hid in Baal's temple, but was found
He was captured alive and taken to Samaria
He allied with Jehu and survived

9.question: What happened to Jezebel when Jehu arrived?
options: She was thrown from the window and trampled
She hid inside the palace until Jehu arrived
She was taken captive to Samaria by Jehu's order
She called her eunuchs to face the crowd

9.question: What was left of Jezebel, fulfilling the prophecy?
options: Only the skull, feet and hands, for the dogs ate her
Only a few charred bones, for the fire consumed all the rest
Only her royal jewels and robes, found intact on the floor
Her entire body, kept whole for a proper burial

10.title: Zeal without a whole heart
10.text: Jehu destroyed Baal from Israel with great zeal, but did not turn from Jeroboam's golden calves. He fought 'foreign' idolatry but kept the 'national' kind: a divided heart.

10.question: What did Jehu demand of Samaria's leaders?
options: The heads of Ahab's seventy sons
A solemn oath of loyalty to the new king
The war chariots and horses of the city
Gold and silver kept in the palace

10.question: What happened to Ahab's seventy sons?
options: They were killed, and their heads piled at the gate
They were taken captive to Samaria, along with the elders
They were all spared and raised by the city's great men
They fled to Syria, under Hazael's protection

10.question: What did Jehu do to Ahaziah's kinsmen whom he met?
options: He killed them
He spared them
He crowned them
He exiled them

10.question: Whom did Jehu take with him 'to see his zeal'?
options: Jehonadab
Elisha
The king of Syria
A priest of Baal

10.question: How did Jehu gather all the worshipers of Baal?
options: By pretending he would hold a great service to Baal
By announcing a solemn sacrifice in the king's name
By promising wealth and positions to all who would come
By summoning them all by force to the palace

10.question: What happened to the gathered worshipers of Baal?
options: They were killed, and Baal's temple destroyed
They were exiled, and Baal's temple was plundered
They were spared, but forced to serve under Jehu
They converted and served the Lord faithfully

10.question: From what sin did Jehu not turn, despite his zeal?
options: From Jeroboam's golden calves
From the idolatry practiced by former kings
From the high places where people still sacrificed
From alliances with foreign kings

10.question: What did Hazael begin to do in Jehu's time?
options: To oppress and shrink Israel's territory
To send armies to guard the distant borders
To make peace treaties with neighboring kings
To rebuild the ancient walls of Samaria

11.title: The line saved by a thread
11.text: Athaliah killed nearly all the royal seed, but princess Jehosheba hid the infant Joash. By this fragile thread, David's house — and the promise of the Messiah — was preserved.

11.question: What did queen Athaliah do to seize the throne?
options: She killed the royal heirs
She bribed the guard captains
She allied with the priests of Baal
She took refuge in Syria

11.question: What did the priest Jehoiada organize to protect the boy-king?
options: The guards and captains in the temple
An ambush set up at the city's main gates
A garrison made up of foreign mercenaries
A secret escape late in the night

11.question: What happened when Joash was crowned?
options: Athaliah cried 'Treason!' and was killed
The people acclaimed the new king in silence
The priests fled quickly into the desert
Jehoiada was wounded in the great battle

11.question: What did the people do after crowning Joash?
options: They renewed the covenant and destroyed Baal's temple
They constructed a new altar on top of the mount of olives
They also crowned a second king to strengthen the throne
They gave the throne back to Athaliah, repentant

12.title: Good while well guided
12.text: Joash did right 'all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him.' The detail reveals a faith leaning on a mentor — and that weakened when that support was gone.

12.question: While he did right, who instructed king Joash?
options: The priest Jehoiada
The prophet Elisha
His mother
The king of Syria

12.question: What great work did Joash order in his reign?
options: To repair the temple of the Lord
To rebuild the altar of sacrifices
To fortify the walls of Jerusalem
To dig new wells for water

12.question: How was the money for the temple work collected?
options: In a chest, and the workers were honest
Through taxes forcibly collected from everyone
By selling sacred temple objects to foreigners
With loans borrowed from the neighbors

12.question: What did Joash do so Hazael would not attack Jerusalem?
options: He gave him the temple treasures
He attacked the Syrian forces first
He asked Egypt's king for military aid
He surrendered the city without a fight

13.title: Life even in the bones
13.text: Years after his death, a body was cast into Elisha's grave; touching the prophet's bones, the dead man revived and stood up — a sign that God's power does not die with his servants.

13.question: What was Jehoahaz's reign like in Israel?
options: He did evil, and Syria oppressed him
He was righteous, and the Lord blessed him
He abolished Baal, and the land had peace
He reigned in peace for many years

13.question: What did the Lord give Israel when Jehoahaz prayed?
options: A deliverer, easing Syria's oppression
Riches brought from the spoils of a foreign war
A new prophet to replace Elisha himself
Abundant rain after a long drought

13.question: What happened to Elisha at the end of his life?
options: He fell sick with the illness he would die of
He was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire
He fled to the desert for fear of the new king
He was cured and lived twenty more years

13.question: What limited king Jehoash's victories, in the episode of the arrows?
options: He struck the ground only three times, instead of more
He shot the arrows far too high and completely missed his aim
He totally refused the arrows that Elisha offered to him
He did not pray before shooting any arrows at all

13.question: What did Jehoash recover from Syria, according to Elisha's word?
options: The cities of Israel that Hazael had taken
The temple, destroyed by the Syrian armies
The Jordan river, once taken by the Ammonites
Samaria, the entire capital city itself

14.title: Justice according to the Law
14.text: Amaziah executed those who killed his father, but spared their children, obeying the Law: 'the fathers shall not die for the children, nor the children for the fathers.' Each answers for his own sin.

14.question: How did Amaziah's reign in Judah begin?
options: He did right, but not like David
He did evil, as his fathers had done
He was right like David, removing all altars
He reigned weakly without conquests

14.question: How did Jehoash of Israel answer Amaziah's challenge?
options: With the parable of the thistle and the cedar, warning against pride
By accepting the challenge with joy and marching quickly to the battle
By sending precious gifts to seal a lasting alliance with the house of Judah
By refusing to answer and hiding himself away in the city of Samaria

14.question: What was the result of the war Amaziah provoked?
options: Judah was defeated; Jerusalem's wall broken and the temple plundered
Israel was defeated; Samaria's wall broken and the temple plundered
Judah won the battle; received gold and hostages from Israel as tribute
There was a truce between the kings and no wall was broken

14.question: How did Amaziah's reign end?
options: He was slain in a conspiracy; his son Azariah reigned
He died peacefully in old age; his son Azariah reigned after
He was deposed by the people and fled to Egypt, never returning
He reigned until dying peacefully of natural illness

14.question: What did Jeroboam II do for Israel?
options: He restored Israel's old borders
He destroyed the old borders and annexed Judah
He conquered new lands never before held by Israel
He lost a large part of the territory

14.question: Why did the Lord use Jeroboam II to save Israel?
options: He saw Israel's bitter affliction and would not yet blot it out
Because Judah had begged for urgent help against common enemies
Because Jeroboam promised to destroy all the high places and idols
Because the people had finally repented of their sins

15.title: The price of pride
15.text: Azariah (Uzziah) reigned well and long, but the Lord struck him with leprosy, and he lived in isolation the rest of his life — according to Chronicles, for usurping the priestly role in the temple.

15.question: What was Azariah's (Uzziah's) long reign in Judah like?
options: He did right, but was struck with leprosy and lived apart
He did evil and was cast out of the throne by the people
He reigned with full justice, never suffering any illness
He was idolatrous and destroyed the temple of the Lord

15.question: What marked the kings of Israel after Jeroboam II?
options: They fell by conspiracies and murders
They ruled with wisdom and lasting peace
They united to drive Assyria away for good
They prospered and multiplied riches

15.question: How did Menahem's reign in Israel begin?
options: With violence, seizing the throne by force
With the unanimous support of priests and elders
Through marriage into the royal family
As the rightful heir to the throne

15.question: What did Menahem do in the face of Assyria's advance?
options: He paid heavy tribute to Pul (Assyria) to keep the throne
He gathered a great army and defeated the Assyrians in battle
He made a secret alliance with Egypt against the Assyrians
He fled to the mountains and abandoned the throne

15.question: How did Pekah come to Israel's throne?
options: He conspired and killed king Pekahiah
He was chosen by the elders of the people
He married the daughter of the previous king
He rose to the throne without dispute

15.question: What did Tiglath-pileser of Assyria begin to do with Israel?
options: He carried part of the people captive
He destroyed all the temples in Israel
He appointed a new puppet king in Samaria
He signed a treaty of peace

15.question: What was Jotham's reign in Judah like?
options: He did right, like his father Uzziah
He did evil, following the high places and idols
He reigned briefly and was deposed by the people
He worshiped the gods of northern Israel

16.title: Ahaz, the opposite of faith
16.text: Ahaz did evil to the point of burning his own son in sacrifice, imitating the pagan nations. Instead of trusting God in danger, he bought Assyria's protection and corrupted the temple.

16.question: What did Ahaz of Judah do, imitating the pagan peoples?
options: He even sacrificed his own son in the fire
He rebuilt the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem
He abolished all the idolatrous cults in his kingdom
He restored the ancient altars of David

16.question: What did Ahaz do to get Assyria's help against his enemies?
options: He bribed it with the temple and palace gold
Formed a military alliance with Egypt against Assyria
Offered sacrifices to the gods of Syria for help
He sent envoys to negotiate with Egypt

16.question: What did Ahaz copy and have built in the temple?
options: A pagan altar he had seen in Damascus
A golden statue he brought from Assyria
A royal throne copied from the Egyptian palace
A high wall he had seen in Nineveh

16.question: What did Ahaz do with the Lord's bronze altar?
options: He moved it aside, putting the new altar in its place
He restored it completely and covered it with pure gold
He destroyed it completely and burned all of its pieces
He covered it with gold and shining silver

17.title: Why Israel fell
17.text: The chapter pauses to explain the fall: Israel sinned against the Lord, followed other gods and the customs of the nations, and did not heed the prophets. The exile was consequence, not chance.

17.question: Who was the last king of the northern kingdom (Israel)?
options: Hoshea
Jeroboam
Jehu
Menahem

17.question: What happened to Samaria and the kingdom of Israel?
options: It fell to Assyria, and the people were carried into exile
It bravely resisted the Assyrian siege for many long years
It made peace with Assyria and kept its complete independence
It quickly rebuilt itself and prospered under a new king

17.question: Why, according to the chapter, was Israel exiled?
options: It sinned and served idols, ignoring the prophets
It refused to pay tribute to its powerful neighboring kings
It formed a military alliance against Judah and Assyria
It always lacked a just and strong king

17.question: What did the Lord do with Israel because of its sins?
options: He rejected it and removed it from his sight, leaving only Judah
He forgave all its sins and immediately restored its whole kingdom
He sent yet another very powerful prophet to warn them one more time
He completely restored the ancient kingdom of the north

17.question: What did Assyria do with the region of Samaria after the exile?
options: It brought in foreign peoples to live there
It left the city completely empty and in ruins
It returned the entire region to the people of Israel
It burned down all the neighboring cities

17.question: What happened to the new inhabitants of Samaria?
options: Lions attacked them; so a priest taught them to fear the Lord
They quickly prospered and built a great new temple of their own
They were exiled again to another far more distant unknown land
They converted immediately and abandoned their old idols

17.question: What became of the religion of the peoples brought to Samaria?
options: They feared the Lord, but also served their own idols
They worshiped only the Lord and abandoned all old customs
They worshiped only idols and completely rejected the true Lord
They abandoned all religion and lived without any faith

17.question: What had the Lord commanded this people?
options: To fear him alone, and no other gods
To build altars on every high mountain
To pay yearly tribute to powerful neighboring kings
To worship many different foreign gods

18.title: When the good becomes an idol
18.text: Hezekiah even broke the bronze serpent Moses had made, for the people had begun to burn incense to it. He called it 'Nehushtan' (a piece of brass): not even what was once sacred may take God's place.

18.question: What was king Hezekiah of Judah like?
options: He did right and removed the idolatrous high places
He was wicked and rebuilt the idolatrous altars of Ahaz
He worshiped Baal and restored the high places his father destroyed
He reigned briefly and made no religious reforms

18.question: What did Hezekiah do to Moses' bronze serpent?
options: He broke it up, for it had become an idol (Nehushtan)
He kept it in the temple as a sacred relic of Moses
He ordered the people to keep offering it incense
He had it melted down to make silver coins

18.question: What did Sennacherib of Assyria do to Judah?
options: He invaded, and Hezekiah even paid him tribute
He signed a lasting peace treaty with the king of Judah
He was defeated and forced to return the captured cities
He fled before fully besieging Jerusalem

18.question: What did Assyria send against Jerusalem?
options: A great army and high officers
Only a letter demanding surrender
Only messengers with a peace proposal
A small group of hidden spies

18.question: What did the officer Rab-shakeh tell the people, by the wall?
options: Not to trust in the Lord or in Egypt
To surrender to Egypt before it was too late
To worship the king of Assyria as their true god
To flee to the neighboring mountains

18.question: Why did Rab-shakeh speak in Hebrew, in a loud voice?
options: To frighten the people on the wall
To negotiate directly with king Hezekiah
To praise Hezekiah before his own servants
Out of respect for Jewish customs

18.question: What argument did Rab-shakeh use for the people to surrender?
options: That no god had saved any nation from Assyria's hand
That Hezekiah had already secretly surrendered to the king of Assyria
That the gods of Judah had already abandoned the people long ago
That Egypt had promised to send an army in relief

19.title: The letter before the Lord
19.text: Hezekiah received Sennacherib's blasphemous letter, went up to the temple and spread it before the Lord, praying: 'Save us, that all the kingdoms may know that you alone are God.' He took the problem to God.

19.question: What did Hezekiah do on hearing Assyria's threats?
options: He tore his clothes and sent to consult the prophet Isaiah
He surrendered immediately and handed over the city's keys
He fled quickly to Egypt seeking refuge and strong military help
He attacked the Assyrian camp by surprise at once

19.question: What did Isaiah tell Hezekiah in the face of the Assyrian threat?
options: Not to fear, for God would act
To surrender before it was too late
To flee to Egypt in search of help
To pay more tribute to Assyria

19.question: What did Hezekiah do with Sennacherib's blasphemous letter?
options: He spread it before the Lord in the temple and prayed
He burned it publicly before the elders of the people
He tore it into pieces and threw it out of the palace
He replied in writing with similar threats

19.question: What did Hezekiah pray to the Lord for?
options: That all might know that He alone is God
That Judah might be free from all Assyrian tribute
That the Assyrian army might be fully forgiven
That his own life might be prolonged

19.question: What did Isaiah prophesy about Sennacherib?
options: That he would not enter the city nor shoot an arrow into it
That he would conquer Jerusalem and make it his new capital
That he would make peace with Hezekiah and withdraw in honor
That he would rule over all the land of Judah for many years

19.question: Why would the Lord defend Jerusalem?
options: For his own sake and for David his servant
For the merit and constant faithfulness of the people
Because of a trade alliance made with Egypt
For no special reason that was revealed

19.question: How was the Assyrian army destroyed?
options: The angel of the Lord struck 185,000 in one night
Hezekiah's army fully defeated them in an open battle
A common plague slowly spread through the entire camp
A violent storm quickly destroyed their tents

20.title: The sign of the shadow
20.text: As a sign that he would live fifteen more years, Hezekiah saw the shadow on the sundial go back ten degrees — God reversed the natural course of time to confirm his promise of healing.

20.question: What did Hezekiah do on learning he would die of his illness?
options: He prayed and wept before the Lord
He summoned the priests to intercede for him
He asked Isaiah to intercede for him
He accepted the sentence with resignation

20.question: What did the Lord grant Hezekiah, with a sign?
options: Fifteen more years of life; the shadow went back
Instant healing and a mighty army to defeat Assyria
Thirty more years of life and a sign in the temple
Complete healing, without any visible sign

20.question: What did Hezekiah show the envoys from Babylon?
options: All his treasures
Only the royal chambers
The letters sent by the king
Only the armory

20.question: What did Isaiah prophesy after Hezekiah displayed the treasures?
options: That all would be carried to Babylon, in the future
That Assyria would conquer Jerusalem within a few years
That Hezekiah would reign in peace for many more years
That the treasures would be restored twofold

21.title: The king who sealed the judgment
21.text: Manasseh rebuilt all his father had destroyed and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood. His reign, the longest and the most wicked, became the decisive reason the Lord decreed Judah's ruin.

21.question: What did Manasseh, son of Hezekiah, do at first?
options: He rebuilt the high places his father had destroyed
He destroyed all the altars that Hezekiah had erected
He consulted the prophets before making any decision
He sought Isaiah for counsel and guidance

21.question: How far did Manasseh's idolatry go?
options: He put idols and altars inside the temple itself, and shed innocent blood
He limited his idolatrous acts only to the neighboring cities, without affecting Jerusalem
He allowed only a few pagan sacrifices discreetly outside the holy city itself
He restricted himself to burning incense outside the sacred temple limits

21.question: What did the Lord announce because of Manasseh?
options: That he would bring disaster on Jerusalem, 'wiping it as a dish'
That he would fully restore the kingdom's glory, as in the days of Solomon
That he would send a great mighty prophet to reform the whole nation
That he would renew the covenant forever with all the people of Judah

21.question: What was Amon, Manasseh's son, like?
options: He also did evil, like his father
He destroyed the idols his father had made
He walked faithfully in the ways of the Lord
He sought God with all his heart

21.question: What happened after Amon was killed by his servants?
options: The people made his son Josiah king
The nobility chose a general to rule instead
The priests took over the governance of the temple
The kingdom fell into total anarchy

22.title: The rediscovered Book
22.text: During the temple repairs, the high priest Hilkiah found the Book of the Law, long forgotten. Its reading shook king Josiah and triggered Judah's greatest religious reform.

22.question: What was the young king Josiah like?
options: He did right and ordered the temple repaired
He followed the idolatrous customs of Manasseh, his grandfather
He worshiped Baal in secret, to please the nobility
He reigned briefly and accomplished nothing

22.question: What was found in the temple during the repairs?
options: The Book of the Law
Hidden gold
An ancient weapon
A throne

22.question: How did Josiah react on hearing the words of the Law?
options: He tore his clothes, in grief and repentance
He ordered the book burned immediately, fearing its contents
He gathered all the people to celebrate a great national feast
He ordered the priests to interpret it

22.question: What did the prophetess Huldah answer Josiah?
options: She confirmed the judgment, but said he would die in peace, for his humility
She said no evil at all would happen while he reigned with justice in the land of Judah
She announced he would fully defeat Babylon and free all the people of Judah forever
She promised he would still reign for a thousand more years in glory

23.title: A king without equal — too late
23.text: Of Josiah it is said there was no king before or after who turned to the Lord with all his heart as he did. Even so, the judgment on Judah, built up by Manasseh, was not revoked.

23.question: What did Josiah do after hearing the Law?
options: He made a covenant to follow the Lord and his commandments
He gathered the priests and ordered the idolatrous high places rebuilt
He sent messengers to ask the king of Egypt for urgent help
He ordered new altars to be built in the temple

23.question: What did Josiah do to the idols and pagan priests?
options: He destroyed them throughout the land
He reinstalled them at new high places throughout the land
He transferred them to the temple in Jerusalem
He spared them out of respect for the people

23.question: What did Josiah do to the idolatrous high places and altars?
options: He defiled and destroyed them
He consecrated them again to pagan worship
He handed them over to the priests of Baal
He repurposed them for other use

23.question: What ancient prophecy did Josiah fulfill by destroying Beth-el's altar?
options: That of the man of God, centuries before, against Jeroboam's altar
That of the prophet Elijah, many centuries later, against Baal's altar
That of King David, many generations before, against Dagon's temple
That of Jeremiah, much later, against Jerusalem's temple

23.question: What celebration did Josiah hold, unlike any since the judges?
options: A great Passover
A national fast
A coronation
A harvest feast

23.question: How did Josiah die?
options: He was killed by Pharaoh Necho, in battle
He was killed by Assyrian soldiers, in an ambush
He was badly wounded and died at Megiddo
He was captured and executed afterward

23.question: What happened to Judah after Josiah's death?
options: It became Egypt's vassal, under imposed kings
It became Babylon's close ally, under a new treaty
It became dependent on Assyria, under heavy tribute
It regained its full political independence

24.title: The announced judgment draws near
24.text: The text is explicit: all this came upon Judah at the Lord's command, because of Manasseh's sins and the innocent blood he had shed. The prophecy of chapter 21 begins to be fulfilled.

24.question: Who subdued Judah, making it a vassal?
options: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon
Nabonidus, king of the ancient Chaldeans
Sennacherib, king of mighty Assyria
Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria

24.question: According to the text, why did these evils come upon Judah?
options: By the Lord's judgment, because of Manasseh's sins
By a broken covenant with Egypt, because of Jehoiakim's sins
By vengeance of the pagan gods, against the chosen people
By ongoing rebellion against mighty imperial Babylon

24.question: What did Babylon do on taking Jerusalem in Jehoiachin's reign?
options: It plundered the temple and carried the elite into exile
It confirmed Jehoiachin as king and returned the temple treasures
It spared the temple but exiled only the princes and eunuchs
It besieged the city and withdrew without taking captives

24.question: Whom did Babylon set up as vassal king in Judah?
options: Zedekiah
Jehoiakim
Josiah
Amon

25.title: A glimmer in the dark
25.text: The book ends in exile, with Jerusalem in ruins. But the final paragraph records that Jehoiachin was released from prison in Babylon and treated with honor — a sign that David's house had not been utterly extinguished.

25.question: What happened during the long siege of Jerusalem?
options: There was severe famine in the city
The city received supplies for months
The Chaldean troops withdrew from the region
The city surrendered right away

25.question: What happened to Zedekiah when the city fell?
options: He was captured, his eyes put out, and taken to Babylon
He was pardoned, kept his throne, and continued ruling all Judah
He was chained and exiled with his whole family far away to Egypt
He was killed in battle, without any trial or sentence

25.question: What did Nebuzar-adan do to the city and the temple?
options: He burned the temple, the palace, and Jerusalem
He rebuilt the temple, the palace, and Jerusalem
He preserved the temple, the palace, and the whole city
He spared only the poor people of the city

25.question: What was carried from the temple to Babylon?
options: The bronze pillars and vessels, and the people into exile
Only the golden vessels and silver, kept safely in the palace
The temple's foundation stones and sacred scrolls, kept there
Only the golden objects, and nothing else besides

25.question: What happened to Gedaliah, set up as governor?
options: He was assassinated, and the remnant fled to Egypt
He was crowned king in Jerusalem, and the people acclaimed him with joy
He was taken to Babylon along with the deposed king under guard
He ruled peacefully and justly until dying of old age

25.question: On what note of hope does the book of 2 Kings end?
options: Jehoiachin was released from prison and treated with honor in Babylon
The temple was fully rebuilt and sacrifices were restored in Jerusalem
The people were allowed to return and rebuild the great city of Jerusalem
God promised to restore the throne of David very soon indeed
